minutes.headline: Task force reviewed the Friday green communities grant, led by the sewer pump project, plus a police hybrid cruiser; next meeting June 3.
minutes.summary: The Green Community Task Force met on Zoom to prepare the town's Green Communities grant application, due Friday, with MRPC's grant writer Karen. Discussion covered the sewer pump and VFD project and its energy-savings calculation, the police hybrid cruiser incentive, school lighting, and training. The group also discussed outreach and the effect of the override. Minutes were approved and the meeting adjourned, each by roll call.

budget_items.what_was_said: Consultants quoted prices that were too high. A contractor working for Unitil offered to do the calculation at no charge by Wednesday.

budget_items.topic: Sewer pump and VFD project cost estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director gave a cost estimate for the project, later refined with freight charges.
An estimated incentive is acceptable in the application if documented. Incentives can cover an overage, as with the street light project.
The paperwork for the cruiser incentive had not reached Karen. She needs the vehicle order form.
Karen said any school lighting would go in if there was room under the ceiling.
The training is still available, at a cost per seat, and two seats were left unused before.
The K9 vehicle is too large to qualify. Specialised equipment raises its price considerably.
Previous grant rounds funded several hybrid cruisers, with a fixed amount per vehicle. The price difference from a conventional cruiser was discussed.
If the sewer project is not ready, the group would wait for the fall rather than submit a small application.
The group could contribute a sum toward a pressing need, as with the sewer project.

budget_items.topic: School utility cost increase and solar credits
budget_items.what_was_said: A member said part of the school utility increase was on paper and that banked solar credits had not been used to offset costs. The solar reporting is still not corrected.

decisions.decision: DPW director will ask the maintenance contractor for a report documenting that the pumps are obsolete, what replaces them and the cost.
The VFDs will be included in the combined sewer project submission.
Chair will talk to Heather and the police chief to get the cruiser order form to Karen.
Priority order agreed: sewer project first, then the police cruiser, then school lighting, then training courses.
The building operator certification topic goes to the other town and school facilities directors, not the DPW.
If the sewer project is not ready by Friday, the group will wait for the fall round.
Next meeting set for June 3, format Zoom or in person still to be decided.
Kim will send the approved and new minutes to the invitation list, including the clerk.
Karen will send the past grant tables to Kim to support outreach about hybrid cruisers and other projects.

what_happened.line: The task force agreed a priority order for the Friday Green Communities application: the sewer pump project first, then the police hybrid cruiser, school lighting and training.
The DPW director will ask the maintenance contractor for a report showing the pumps are obsolete, what replaces them and the cost.
The variable frequency drives will be folded into the combined sewer project submission, and a Unitil contractor offered a free energy-savings calculation.
If the sewer project is not ready by Friday, the group will wait for the fall grant round rather than submit a small application.
The next meeting is set for June 3; no vote was taken on any substantive item, and the format is still undecided.

why_it_matters: The Green Communities grant can pay for energy projects such as sewer pump upgrades and hybrid police cruisers, so what the town submits this round decides which of those get state money rather than local tax dollars.
A missed Friday deadline moves the sewer project to the fall round, which delays any energy savings and any grant offset to the cost of the work.
